---
title: "Airform"
description: "dbt-style, version-controlled SQL modeling for Oxygen"
---

**Airform** handles the transform step: dbt-style, version-controlled SQL models
that turn raw tables into clean, tested ones. It lives alongside your agents,
automations, and semantic model in the same workspace, and is validated and
deployed through the standard Git flow, so the tables your
[semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) builds on are modeled
deterministically, not assembled ad hoc. Airform works in three stages:

- **Compile** resolves each model's Jinja, `ref()`, and `source()` calls into
  plain SQL, and works out the dependency graph between models.
- **Build** runs the compiled SQL on your warehouse, one model at a time in
  dependency order, so every model reads tables that are already up to date.
- **Test** runs the project's schema and data tests against the tables it
  built.

## Why model with Airform

- **Version-controlled transforms.** Your models are code, reviewed and deployed
  through the same Git flow as the rest of your project.
- **Tested tables.** Transforms land clean, tested tables, so the semantic model
  compiles over a dependable foundation.
- **Reviewable SQL.** Every model compiles to plain SQL that you can read before
  it runs, so there is no hidden logic between your files and your tables.
- **One workspace.** Modeling sits next to agents, automations, and the semantic
  model, with no separate tool or Python environment to context-switch into.

## The project

An Airform project follows dbt conventions, so existing dbt projects work
largely unchanged. Each project is a folder under `modeling/` in your
workspace, and Oxygen discovers every folder that contains a
`dbt_project.yml`:

```
your-workspace/
├── config.yml
└── modeling/
    └── my_project/
        ├── dbt_project.yml
        ├── profiles.yml
        ├── oxy.yml        # maps each dbt target to a database in config.yml
        ├── models/
        └── seeds/
```

`oxy.yml` is what ties a project to your workspace: it maps each dbt target in
`profiles.yml` to a database already connected in `config.yml`, so Airform
reuses the workspace's connections and secrets instead of keeping its own.

## Compile, build, and test

Open **Modeling** in the IDE sidebar to see every discovered project and run
it:

- **Compile** shows the plain SQL each model resolves to, without running
  anything.
- **Run** compiles and builds models in dependency order, and accepts dbt node
  selectors such as `+my_model` or `tag:daily` to build part of the graph.
- **Test** runs the project's schema and data tests.
- **Seed** loads the project's CSV seed files.

## Lineage

Because Airform compiles the whole project into a graph, it can show both the
model-level DAG, which models feed which, and column-level lineage, which
upstream columns each output column comes from. That makes it possible to see
what a change will affect before you make it.

## Supported warehouses

Airform builds models on a database connected in `config.yml`: Snowflake,
BigQuery, Postgres, Redshift, MySQL, ClickHouse, DuckDB (file databases), and
MotherDuck. The [modeling reference](/guide/build/semantic-model/modeling) lists
how each one is configured.
